tasks.title: Pond survey in the city park
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.subject: Pond survey in the city park
paragraphs: As you know, our class is helping with a pond survey in the city park next Saturday. We need to decide on the main goal of the survey. Should we focus on counting the different types of wildlife in the pond, or on testing the water quality to see if it's healthy? Which do you think is more important and why?
Also, we need to choose one practical task for volunteers. Would you prefer to help with setting up equipment near the pond, or with recording the data we collect?
Finally, can you suggest one way to encourage more students to join the survey?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which main goal you prefer and explain why.
Choose a practical task (setting up equipment or recording data) and give a reason.
Suggest one way to encourage more students to join.
Ask Ms. Rivera about the time the survey starts.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Ms. Rivera using all the notes.

tasks.title: Pond survey article
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: A pond survey is happening in our city park next Saturday.
Do you think this survey will help protect urban wildlife?
What is the most interesting thing you would like to learn from the survey?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it on our website!

tasks.title: Pond survey story
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
"When the programme coordinator handed me the clipboard, I had no idea that the pond survey would change everything."
